campaign.title: M1 lower-GAR exact signed reduced-Farey scalar gate

resource_policy.literature_policy: No theorem-name continuation. External input is admissible only after an exact theorem card audits coefficient class, primitive supports, absolute-value placement, centre uniformity, and a complete R-power ledger. The primary objective is a direct actual-scalar derivation.

frozen_target.question: Can the exact lower-GAR scalar be bounded by R X^epsilon in its reduced-Farey form, or can its exact scalar square be reduced to a strictly smaller signed nonzero-determinant survivor, without passing through the rejected separated k-square function; if not, what is the first exact resonance, completion, stationary, directionality, self-return, or capacity obstruction?
frozen_target.reference_formula: F_N=sum_(2<=b<=y, b odd) lambda_b sum_(1<=a<b,(a,b)=1) e(aN/b)J_(R,y)(a/b), lambda_b=chi_4(b)b^(-1)sum_(g<=y/b)chi_4(g)/g, R=X^(1/4), y=floor(sqrt(X)), N=floor(X), with target |F_N|<<_epsilon R X^epsilon. Its exact square has phase e(N(ab'-a'b)/(bb')) and target R^2=y.
quantities: J_(R,y)(t)=eta(yt)V_low(4R^2t^2)/t on the small positive arc, extended smoothly by zero and periodically, with J(0)=0
reducing h/d=a/b aggregates all odd lifts into lambda_b before any norm
the b=1 centre vanishes because J(0)=0; determinant zero in the exact scalar square is equality of reduced fractions
the diagonal target is O(yX^epsilon); same-denominator unequal numerators remain off diagonal and require a separate control
the exact scalar has absolute capacity y=R^2 and target R; its exact square has absolute capacity y^2 and target y
the Round-127 uncentered k-energy is false and the centered k-energy is a stronger separated norm; neither is the frozen mechanism
all floors, primitive numerators, lift character, literal profile, support endpoints, both signs, and real-X uniformity are retained

completion_criteria: Derive the exact reduced-Farey scalar from the literal flat lower cone, including the missing 1/d, odd lifts, b=1 centre, primitive numerators, profile, and both signs.
Prove and price the exact scalar-square diagonal and the same-denominator unequal-numerator sector before estimating cross-denominator determinants.

For every determinant split, character pairing, reciprocity, Poisson, B-process, or stationary step, retain the actual lambda_b and J profile and return the result to the R target uniformly for every real X.
Test exact and near phase-one families, fourth-power centres, denominators near y, divisors of N, numerator endpoints, stationary dual modes, and support crossings.

Preserve scalar directionality: no dyadic positive k-energy, coefficient-uniform arbitrary array, rowwise or determinantwise modulus, centre averaging, or full-circle Gauss estimate may substitute for the literal scalar.
Close under exactly one label: target_bound, strict_signed_farey_reduction, or signed_farey_no_go.
Make no complete GAR, M9-M1, M9-M2, endpoint, M9, quarter, or exponent promotion unless every corresponding owner and dependency is proved.

tasks.target: Derive and exploit the exact reduced-Farey scalar and its actual scalar-square determinant form to prove the R target, a strict smaller signed survivor, or the first exact arithmetic or transform obstruction.
required_output: An exact scalar and scalar-square dictionary with a complete R-power ledger.
A target estimate, strict owner-complete signed survivor, or first exact scalar obstruction.
Write only the assigned report and make no graph or shared-state edit.

tasks.target: Independently decide from the exact scalar statement whether its character-lift coefficient and determinant phase prove the R bound, yield a strict signed reduction, or encounter a rigorous coherent or self-return obstruction.
excluded_context: all Round-121 through Round-138 nonblind artifacts
required_output: A self-contained proof attempt with exact resonance and capacity controls.
A target estimate, strict signed survivor, or first exact no-go step.
Write only the assigned report and make no graph or shared-state edit.

tasks.target: Hostilely audit the exact scalar reduction, diagonal and same-denominator sectors, resonance families, and every determinant or stationary transform for direction loss, hidden capacity, self-return, circularity, and downstream overclaim.
required_output: An equation-by-equation directionality and capacity audit of every proposed scalar transform.
Certification, strict reduction, scope correction, or rigorous no-go.
Write only the assigned report and make no graph or shared-state edit.

closing_assessment.main_result: The exact integerized lower scalar square equals one signed cross-denominator residual plus O_epsilon(yX^epsilon). The complete same-denominator block and both ordinary and character-adjusted carrier collars of width y^(-2) are target-square-safe. Determinant fibres have an unavoidable aspect loss; exact hard-endpoint Poisson has a principal R^(3/2) ledger, a unique target-safe exact radical channel, and full nonprincipal owners; repeated transforms self-return. The residual O_epsilon(yX^epsilon) estimate remains open.

review_seams.requirement: The literal flat cone, reduced fractions, odd lift sum, primitive numerator, b=1 centre, profile, floors, and both signs are reproduced exactly.
The exact scalar square is distinguished from the rejected separated k-energy; determinant zero and same-denominator nonzero determinants are priced separately.
Exact and near phase-one families, fourth-power centres, denominators dividing N, and numerator/support endpoints are tested with the actual character-lift coefficient.
Every pairing, reciprocity, Poisson, determinant-fibre, or stationary step retains coefficients and correction owners and is classified as contraction, strict reduction, or self-return.
Every bound returns to R, and no rowwise modulus, arbitrary coefficient norm, positive k-energy, centre average, or circular full-circle estimate replaces the actual scalar.
Only the lower-GAR scalar may change; GAR, blockwise M1, M9-M1, all M2 parents, endpoint uniformity, M9, the quarter theorem, and both global exponents retain their owners.
